key_insight: A foundation "chemical language" model trained on a large corpus of natural-product structures learns reusable structural and biosynthetic motifs, enabling accurate transfer to a variety of downstream natural-product mining tasks with limited labels.
problem_solved: Natural products are chemically diverse and underrepresented in labeled datasets; existing models trained on synthetic compounds often fail to capture natural-product-specific patterns needed for mining, prediction, and generation.
method: Assemble a large, curated corpus of natural-product molecular representations (e.g., SMILES/graph encodings) to reflect biosynthetic diversity.
Pretrain a foundation chemical-language model with self-supervised objectives to learn recurrent substructures and context-dependent chemistry.
Fine-tune and evaluate the pretrained model on downstream tasks (mining, bioactivity/property prediction, candidate generation) to demonstrate transferability.
impact: Provides ML practitioners with a specialized pretrained model that reduces labeled-data needs and improves performance for natural-product discovery, annotation, and generative design—accelerating workflows in drug discovery and natural-product research.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: dataset → pretraining (chemical-language model) → fine-tuning → downstream tasks

Bar chart comparing downstream task performance (pretrained vs. baseline) plus example generated candidate molecules
paper_title: Learning the chemical language of natural products
paper_authors: Xu Guo, Celia M. Rava, Allison S. Walker
